act_title: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule

quests.title: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule

dialogue.t: Whew...
That's the last of the monsters around here, right?
You okay, Odette? You fought extra hard today...
I'm fine. It's just...

dialogue.sit: You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to.

dialogue.t: No, I'm just trying to find the right words.
This is where I used to practice dancing when I was little.
Out in the wild?
Well, most of the time, it was in a studio full of mirrors.
But, every so often, I would practice outside. I love dancing in nature. It reminds me of the true essence of the art form — celebrating the beauty in this world.
Ohh! Is that why you took on this mission? Because you wanted to keep this spot peaceful?
That's part of the reason.
It's... because of the Black Snow Swan.
The ballet?
Yes. I practiced it a lot when I was little, but I didn't get to perform it on stage in the end. That was a big disappointment for a long time.
It's about a snow swan whose feathers are a different color than everyone else, right?
That's right. I felt so sorry for the black snow swan back then. It suffered such an unfair fate just because of how it was born.
It deserved to live a normal life alongside its companions, but it couldn't...
Actually, when I was little, the black snow swan was my least favorite role in the ballet. I didn't want to be anything like her...
But fate always has a way of playing tricks on us. The more I wanted to be a dazzling, white snow swan onstage, the closer my real life came to the black swan.

dialogue.sit: (She must be talking about her life as a member of both the Fatui and the Rokot...)

dialogue.t: I have a much greater appreciation for the character now.
But thinking about what I felt as a child helps me reflect on how far I've come. I hoped it might help me better interpret the character in the ballet itself.
So that's why you thought of coming here...
Hm... do you know how the Black Snow Swan's story ends?
She stops trying to fit in with the flock and lives on proudly in solitude.
After that, she flies higher than any other snow swan. In the end, the pure white clouds embrace her, and she goes to a place no white-feathered snow swan could ever reach.
That's a beautiful ending.
Yes. Solitary, yet beautiful.
Well, after hearing all that, Paimon thinks you can pull it off for sure! We'll be cheering for you!
Thank you...
But before that, I should focus on the work I'm doing for the Fatui.
